orders.text:
SA No. 40 of 2016
Hon’ble Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.
Mr. Sudhir Kumar, Advocate for 
the appellants. 
Mr. Tapan Singh, Advocate for the 
respondent. 
Having heard the rival 
contentions, it transpires that initially, an 
O.S. No.395 of 2006 was filed seeking 
cancellation of the Sale Deed dated 30th
January, 2006. Such Suit was decreed on 
27.09.2012 by the Trial Judge in addition 
to an injunction order was also issued to 
the defendant not to create interfere in 
the possession and title of the plaintiff 
pertaining to the property, in dispute. 
The judgment of Trial Judge was 
appealed and First Appellate Court, vide 
its order dated 15.02.2016, was 
dismissed the Suit. 
It has been argued that the First 
Appellate Court has decided the Issue 
No.1 holding that the Civil Court did not 
have jurisdiction to adjudicate this 
matter because questioned property was 
purely agricultural one, so, litigation 
pending before the Civil Court is barred 
under Section 331 of Zamindari Abolition 
Act. 
After deciding the Issue No.1, 
First Appellate Court went further ahead 
and decided the Issue No.2 holding that 
the questioned Sale Deed was executed in 
exchange of due consideration. 
It has been argued that once it 
was held by the First Appellate Court 
expressing the lack of jurisdiction of the 
Civil Court to decide such a controversy, 
then it must not have expressed its own 
view regarding validity of the Sale Deed, 
as indicated above.  On this point, the second appeal 
is admitted for hearing. 
Following substantial questions 
of law is formulated:- 
“(1). Whether the learned lower 
Appellate Court was justified in holding 
that the Civil Court has no jurisdiction to 
try and decide the suit without 
considering that the names of the 
plaintiffs-appellants was recorded in the 
revenue records on the date of suit? 
(2). Whether the learned lower 
Appellate Court was justified in holding 
that the impugned sale deed had been 
executed for a valuable consideration? 
(3). Whether the learned lower 
Appellate Court was justified in 
dismissing the suit of the plaintiffs￾appellants after holding that the Civil 
Court has no jurisdiction to hear and 
decide the suit?” 
Meanwhile, both the parties 
shall maintain the status-quo at the 
spot and they will not create any third 
party interest on the property, in 
question, in any manner, whatsoever. 
Stay application (CLMA 
1991/2016) stands disposed of 
accordingly. 
Call the LCR. 
List in the last week of May, 
2016. 
 (Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.) 
Nadim
 21.03.2016

COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
SA No.40 of 2015
Hon’ble Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.
Present Mr. Sudhir Kumar and Mr. H.M. 
Raturi, counsel for the appellant.
2. None is present for the respondent. 
3. This is Misc. Application (IA No.1992 of 
2023) filed by the appellant praying therein to 
summon the respondent for his appearance in person 
for non-compliance of the order dated 21.03.2016 
passed by this Court.
4. Counsel for the appellant would submit that 
vide order dated 21.03.2016 the Co-ordinate Bench 
of this Court had directed the parties to maintain the 
status quo at the spot and not to create any third 
party interest on the property in question; that, 
despite the order dated 21.03.2016 the 
respondent/defendant executed the sale deed of the 
property in question on 28.08.2023 in favour of Shri 
Shukhpal Singh S/o Mannu Singh R/o Badamawala, 
Tehsil Vikasnagar, Dehradun and Shri Shailendra 
Singh S/o Mange Singh R/o 352 Basantpur, 
Mahavir Hospital Lane Vikasnagar, Dehradun for
consideration of ₹46,00,000/-. Hence, this 
application under Order 39 Rule 2-A r/w 151 C.P.C. 
for initiating the contempt proceedings against the 
respondent/defendant. 
5. Issue notice to the respondent/defendant of 
IA No.1992 of 2023 directing him to appear in 
person on 17.10.2023 and to file reply to this 
application before the Court within one week of 
receiving the notice.
6. Put up on 17.10.2023. 
(Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.) 
 21.09.2023
BS

COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
SA No.40 of 2016
Hon’ble Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.
Present Mr. Sudhir Kumar, counsel for the 
appellants. 
2. Present Mr. Deepak Sharma, counsel for the 
respondent through V.C.
3. On the last date of hearing, notice was issued 
to the respondent/defendant to appear in person as 
the application (IA No. 1992 of 2023) was moved 
by the appellants/plaintiffs; that, despite the
interim order dated 21.03.2016 of the Coordinate 
Bench to maintain status quo at the spot and not to 
create any third party interest over the property in 
question, the respondent/defendant executed a 
sale-deed of the property in question on
28.08.2023 in favour of persons, namely, Sukhpal 
Singh S/o Mannu Singh R/o Badamawala, Tehsil 
Vikas Nagar, Dehradun and Shailendra Singh S/o 
Mange Singh R/o 352 Basantpur, Mahavir 
Hospital Lane Vikasnagar, Dehradun, but 
respondent/defendant is not present in person as 
directed. 
4. Learned counsel for the respondent/defendant 
would submit that the respondent/defendant is an 
old age person and physically not able to move,
therefore, he could not appear before the Court 
however, no document of illness is placed on 
record. 
5. The illness or old age does not give any 
license to flout the order of the Court. Learned 
counsel for the respondent/defendant is not able to 
submit whether the sale-deed of the property in 
question was executed on 28.08.2023 by the 
respondent/defendant in favour of Sukhpal Singh 
S/o Mannu Singh R/o Badamawala, Tehsil Vikas  Nagar, Dehradun and Shailendra Singh S/o Mange 
Singh R/o 352 Basantpur, Mahavir Hospital Lane 
Vikasnagar, Dehradun in consideration of Rs. 
46,00,000/- notwithstanding the interim order 
dated 21.03.2016 passed by the Coordinate 
Bench, as stated above.. 
6. In the above facts and circumstances, it 
appears to this Court that respondent/defendant is
whiling away the time with ulterior motive. 
7. Issue notice to the defendant/respondent to 
explain as to why the property of the 
defendant/respondent should not be attached and 
why he should not be detained in civil 
imprisonment for a term of three months,
returnable within two weeks from today. 
8. Issue notice to Sukhpal Singh S/o Mannu 
Singh R/o Badamawala, Tehsil Vikas Nagar, 
Dehradun and Shailendra Singh S/o Mange Singh 
R/o 352 Basantpur, Mahavir Hospital Lane 
Vikasnagar, Dehradun to place the facts before the 
Court. 
9. Meanwhile, Sukhpal Singh and Shailendra 
Sailendra Singh are restrained from creating any 
third party interest, alienating the property and
transferring the possession of the suit property in 
favour of any other person if any sale-deed as 
alleged was executed on 28.08.2023 in their favour 
by the respondent/defendant. 
10. List this matter on 3rd November, 2023. 
 
(Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.) 
 17.10.2023
Kaushal

20.03.2026 SA No.40 of 2016
Hon’ble Siddhartha Sah, J.
Mr. H.M. Raturi, learned counsel (through 
V.C.) and Mr. Ghanshyam Joshi, learned counsel for 
the appellants. 
2. Mr. Sandeep Kothari, learned counsel for the 
applicant in impleadment application (IA No.1993 
of 2025). 
3. Perusal of the order sheet dated 21.03.2016 in 
the present case reveals that this second appeal was 
admitted on the said date and an interim order was 
also passed to the effect that, in the meantime, both 
the parties shall maintain status-quo at the spot and 
they will not create any third party interest in the 
property, in question, in any manner, whatsoever.
4. The order dated 21.03.2016 further reveals 
that the respondent Basant Singh, was duly 
represented by Mr. Tapan Singh, Advocate, at the 
time of passing of the said order. In fact, Mr. Tapan 
Singh, Advocate, appeared in the appeal on various 
dates, inter alia, 27.07.2016, 26.10.2016, 14.07.2017 
(through brief holder), 17.08.2017, 15.09.2017, and 
08.12.2017.
5. Perusal of the order dated 17.10.2023 would 
reveal that an order was passed for issuing notice to 
the defendant/respondent to explain as to why the 
property of the defendant/respondent should not be 
attached and why he should not be detained in civil 
imprisonment for a term of three months.
6. The office note dated 25.10.2023 reveals that, 
in compliance of the order dated 17.10.2023, an
administrative notice was issued to the 
defendant/respondent. The service report dated 
19.02.2023 reveals that the respondent Basant 
Singh, was served personally. Despite service of 
notice, there is nothing on record to suggest that the  respondent Basant Singh, has filed any explanation 
to the said show-cause notice so far.
7. In view of the above, a show-cause notice is 
issued to the respondent Basant Singh, as to why he 
should not be detained in civil imprisonment for 
committing contempt of the order dated 21.03.2016 
passed by this Court. The said notice be served upon 
the respondent Basant Singh, through the Additional 
District Judge, Vikasnagar, Dehradun.
8. The Registry is directed to do the needful.
9. List on 28.05.2026. 
(Siddhartha Sah, J.) 
 20.03.2026
BS

SA No. 40 of 2016
Ganpat and another .…… Appellants
Vs.
Basant Singh ……Respondent
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Mr. H.M. Raturi, Advocate for the 
appellants.
Mr. Deepak Sharma, Advocate for the 
respondent through video conferencing.
Mr. Sandeep Kothari, Advocate for the 
applicant in Impleadment Application No. 1993 
of 2025.
On 21.03.2016, when the appeal was 
admitted, the Court directed the parties to 
maintain status quo and not to create any third 
party interest in the property in question in 
any manner whatsoever.
It appears that thereafter the respondent 
Basant Singh, S/o Sri Jairam, R/o Baluwala, 
Pargana Pachwa Doon, District Dehradun 
transferred the property by way of executing 
sale deed on 28.08.2023 in favour of Sri 
Sukhpal Singh and Sri Shailendra Singh for 
consideration of Rs.46 Lakh. It is, thereafter, 
on 21.09.2023, the appellants moved an 
application under Order 39 Rule 2A read with 
151 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 for 
resetting the contempt proceeding against the 
respondent. 
The respondent was required to file 
objection, which he is evading, as he has yet 
not filed any objection. Meanwhile, the 
purchasers Sri Sukhpal Singh and Sri 
Shailendra Singh have also been directed by 
the Court not to transfer the property in favour 
of any other persons. Sri Sukhpal Singh and 
Sri Shailendra Singh are before the Court now. 
Notices were issued to them. Since Sri Sukhpal Singh and Sri 
Shailendra Singh have been issued notices and 
they have been directed not to alienate their 
property in suit. They need to be impleaded in 
the second appeal.
Let they be impleaded as respondent nos. 
2 and 3. They have already been represented.
The appellant shall file an amended memo 
of appeal.
It appears that the respondent has 
willfully disobeyed the order of the Court dated 
21.03.2016, when he was directed not to 
transfer the property in suit.
Now there are two courses open against 
him under Order 39 Rule 2A of the Code, one 
by way of attaching his property and second by 
sending him to civil prison.
First and foremost, the Court would 
explore the possibility of attaching his 
property, if any.
Learned counsel for the appellants 
submits that he does not have the details of the 
property of the respondent Basant Singh.
Let a copy of this order be forwarded to 
the Collector, Dehradun, who shall give details 
of the property registered in the name of the 
respondent Basant Singh. The Collector, 
Dehradun shall submit a report to this Court 
on or before 23.07.2026.
List on 23.07.2026 for final hearing after 
fresh cases.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.) 
 03.07.2026
Jitendra
